summary: The Read Restrictions Sync on 18 August 2026 had three items. The first was nested field handling and conflict resolution, with a mailing list thread and a comparison of industry prior art. The second, raised by Sung, was the protocol for enhancing ReadRestrictions after a v1 release; Laurent and Russell argued that capability negotiation should not be allowed, because a client that can opt in to a version could choose a less secure representation of the same policy. The third was a walk through the proofs of concept for Iceberg Generics, Spark and Trino.

topics.title: Nested field handling and conflict resolution
topics.summary: The group discussed how read restrictions handle nested fields and how conflicting policies are resolved. The notes link the mailing list thread and a document comparing industry prior art on nested-field policy conflict resolution. No outcome is recorded.

topics.title: Protocol for enhancing ReadRestrictions after v1
topics.summary: Sung raised how features should be added to ReadRestrictions after the v1 release. Laurent and Russell made the point that if a client can opt in to a version and advertise it, and there are different representations of the same policy, the client can opt in to a less secure version. Their position was that capability negotiation should not be allowed.

topics.title: Proofs of concept: Iceberg Generics, Spark and Trino
topics.summary: The agenda had a walk through the proofs of concept: an end-to-end one for Iceberg Generics, an end-to-end one for Apache Spark, and a document on the Trino code flow. The notes record no discussion.
